reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 19 close: SPX -8.52% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52, -6.08% below its 50-day and -2.34% below its 200-day; SMH -33.39% from its high and NVDA -40.02%, both below their Zone 2 floors; VIX 28.44 at its 5-day high; HY OAS 3.47 calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4. Episode data is fresh (through Nov 19), and the Nov 20 pre-market tape (VIX 30.99, NVDA $140.76 pre-market vs its $145.98 close) extends the selloff into a seventh day.
reaction.invalidation: A daily SPX close back above its 50-day (7,640.19) with SMH and NVDA both reclaimed into Zone 2 and VIX below 25 would void the Watch stance; conversely, HY OAS above 4% with SPX below 7,000 would void the 'correction, not regime break' read and the ladder with it.

ladder.response: No buying; the staged-selling plan arms Stage 1 only on a strength day — nothing sells into the break; hold bills.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below 7,000, or SMH below $430, or NVDA below $130

ladder.response: Treat it as a bull trap: no chasing the first bounce; entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict, and any probe is sized as a probe, not a tranche.
ladder.trigger: A bounce carries SPX into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone (SMH 580-600) and fails there

ladder.response: Stand-down extends and Tranche A/B triggers are void until credit calms (HY OAS back below 4%) and VIX closes below 25.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4%, or VIX closes above 35

ladder.response: Tranche A re-arms (25% deployment per the ladder); below the floors, the setup is broken, not cheaper.
ladder.trigger: SMH and NVDA both close back inside Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

reaction.trapRisk: The first bounce is likely to run straight into the failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820, SMH 580-600) — that is where the trap lives. Do not chase it: NVDA's pre-market slide to $140.76 from its $145.98 close shows how fast entries are punished inside a falling tape. Entries are sized only after the failure-zone retest gives its verdict, and the 20-day ceilings on the opportunity board are not the entry trigger — the zone reclaim is.

strategyPosture: Watch — stand-down is in force: VIX 28.44 is above the 25 stand-down line, SMH and NVDA sit below their Zone 2 floors, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4. No new deployment; hold existing positions and bills, and let the tape prove a bottom or a zone reclaim before any tranche arms.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking: if the Mag7 unwind drags index breadth with it, rotation becomes rollover. The tell is credit — while HY OAS holds below 4% and lending stays loose, the read stays rotation; a spread breakout above 4% flips it.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names sit 20.89% below their 52-week highs on average against 8.4% for SPY — a 12.49-point divergence gap — with NVDA the weakest at -40% and AAPL the strongest at -3.2%. But bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.47 and calm, not cracking. SPX itself is -8.52% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52 — a correction on the index's own terms, not a crash.
themes.label: Mag7 unwind: rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break — the S&P is down six straight days and the AI leaders are in freefall — and the fear is that index leadership is collapsing into a general rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4%, or the Mag7-SPY divergence gap widening past 15 points.

themes.counterRead: Trailing revenue is not forward demand, and the market is discounting a lower forward multiple until the demand question is answered — so the gap is a watchlist, not a buy. The ladder's own rule governs: SMH below $470 and NVDA below $175 means the setup is broken, not cheaper, and no tranche arms until both reclaim Zone 2. Insiders are nibbling at the trough (Rockwell $1.55M, Vistra $1.17M, Kratos $0.2M, Eaton $0.17M) — a toehold signal, not confirmation.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data says otherwise: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year, Lam Research 131.3%, Broadcom 55%, Palantir 56.2%, Datadog 27.7% and MongoDB 22.8%, while the stocks sit 30-54% below their highs. The dislocation table classifies most of these declines as sentiment-driven or multiple compression, not earnings deterioration, and revenue inflection reads RECOVERY across the top names. Datadog pairs 27.7% revenue growth with an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% free-cash-flow margin at 44.6% below its high; Onto Innovation grows 41.5% at 49.3% below its high.
themes.label: AI complex: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market is pricing the AI buildout as if demand is rolling over — SMH is down a third from its high and NVDA 40% — and the narrative is that the capex cycle has broken.
themes.watchFor: SMH and NVDA daily closes back inside Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185).

themes.counterRead: Spreads are a coincident read and can gap; the equity drawdown is the leading edge, and the Nov 20 pre-market tape (VIX 30.99) shows the selloff extending into a seventh day. The line is 4% on HY OAS — above it, the 'equity repricing, not a funding event' read fails and the stand-down extends.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.47 and explicitly calm — not cracking — and the mechanical tally's only confirmed signal of four is credit calm. The 2Y/10Y curve is +0.27 (uninverted), the 10-year is 5.07% and the 2-year 4.80% with the funds rate at 3.88%, and 10-year breakeven inflation is 2.16% — a restrictive-rate regime, not a credit event. The VIX at 28.44 is at its 5-day high, up 52.09% in five days, while spreads have not moved with it.
themes.label: Credit has not confirmed the equity panic
themes.narrative: With the VIX at 28.44 and the S&P down six straight days, the tape implies a funding-stress event is underway.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4%, or the VIX closing above 35.

themes.counterRead: None of this disproves the underlying theses — it is beta and volatility decay doing their job — but it sets the sizing reality: a 3x levered position loses a third when QQQ loses an eighth in a month, and there is no averaging down into the fall while the tape is still making lower lows. The gold hedge failing at the same time means the portfolio has no working diversifier right now.
themes.dataAnchor: TQQQ is -36.39% in one month against QQQ's -12.72%, CONL -66.71%, BMNR -38.81%, and the crypto pair is down with it (Bitcoin -20.43%, Dogecoin -25.95% in a month). Even the diversifier is correlating: IAU is -13.91% in a month and -4.37% on the day as gold falls with everything else. SPY itself is only -8.3% in a month — the damage is concentrated exactly where the leverage and concentration live, which is what those positions are built to do in a downtrend.
themes.label: Leveraged and thematic holdings take the full drawdown
themes.narrative: The portfolio's risk sleeve looks like the thesis is broken — TQQQ, CONL and BMNR are down 36-67% in a month while the index is down 8%.
themes.watchFor: TQQQ's one-month slide (-36.39%) flattening while QQQ stabilizes, or IAU's -13.91% one-month slide flattening.

themes.counterRead: Rates and equities agree that policy is restrictive, so there is no divergence to exploit here — the read is aligned, and the only question is whether the December meeting relieves the pressure or confirms it. A 10-year that keeps climbing into the meeting keeps the derating going; a dovish lean is what would let the AI complex reclaim its zones.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year printed 5.07% on Nov 18, the 30-year 5.41%, the 2-year 4.80% and the real 10-year 2.91% — the long end is doing the tightening while the funds rate sits at 3.88% and the 2s10s curve is +0.27, uninverted. The calendar agrees the December meeting is the next decision point: the FOMC decision Dec 8-9 and CPI Nov on Dec 10 are both HIGH-signal watch events, with PCE Oct on Nov 25 as the near-term print.
themes.label: Rates at the top of the range into the December Fed
themes.narrative: The market's read is that rates are the pressure — the 10-year above 5% is what is derating every long-duration growth name.
themes.watchFor: The Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and the Dec 10 CPI print, with the 10-year's direction into the meeting as the tell.

watchFor: SMH daily close back at or above $470 (Zone 2 floor) and NVDA close at or above $175.
VIX daily close below 25 (stand-down lifts) versus above 30 (escalation).
HY OAS above 4% (regime-break leg) versus holding at or below 3.5%.
SPX daily close versus 7,300 (prior bottom-call line) and versus its 200-day at 7,348.02.
Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI print; PCE Oct on Nov 25.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes in the AI complex: either SMH and NVDA reclaim their Zone 2 floors ($470 and $175) and re-arm Tranche A, or the Dec 8-9 FOMC / Dec 10 CPI disappoints and the selloff extends toward the next zone down — the pre-market tape (VIX 30.99, NVDA $140.76 pre-market vs its $145.98 close) already points to a seventh straight down day unless the open reverses.
